title: Writing the 'Minnie the Moocher' introduction overnight
summary: Cab asked for an arrangement; Thomas wrote an eight-bar intro and ending on strips of paper.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: So we was going down to record the next day, and that night before we was going to record the next day, Cab came to me and said, "Foots, make an arrangement on 'Minnie The Moocher.'" Because I had heard it two or three times, and I'd seen it.
It just had a whole lot of notes in it, it didn't make no kind of sense...

I can't... The melody of "Minnie The Moocher" went "Here's a girl named Minnie The Moocher, She's a low-down hoochie-koocher..." [SINGS REFRAIN] And the name of this song was "Willie The Weeper." They had lyrics to it, "Willie The Weeper," but he changed it to "Minnie The Moocher." So I got up the next morning. I used to...I went to sleep... I could always write better when I was fresh. So I got up about an hour earlier, and went to my piano -- and the melody just started to come to me. I have to admit that Harold Arlen had a song called "Get Happy" -- [SINGS REFRAIN]. And see, I had got an idea of repetition through hearing that. So I just went to the piano, and the melody just came to me -- [SINGS REFRAIN OF 'GET HAPPY' UNTIL...] I

used the last two bars of "Willie The Weeper." So that melody just came to me, and I wrote it out, and to this day I can't tell you how I had this repetition and sequence in it. Then after I wrote that introduction, I said to myself, "I'll just use that same thing to the ending, and just end it off.. [SINGS REFRAIN] I said, "We'll use that for the introduction and the ending." Because I had heard a couple of songs that was doing that.

So in those days, to make it cheap, so it didn't cost a whole lot of money, I didn't even use every instrument on a short sheet of paper. I just took my two sheets of paper and made little strips of it. Because I didn't have but eight bars repeating it... So I just put it in the saxophone case, and went on down to the recording studio.
